profile.research_note:
Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 42 (TierPoint missing-address campaign): found this generic row could represent any of three distinct Saint Louis area buildings, ruled out one via coordinates but declined to choose between the remaining two absent precise geocoding, flagged for future resolution, traced and dated the companys Argo Infrastructure Partners ownership and its own January 2025 acquisition by Apollo Global Management, which the registry had not previously recorded with a citable source. research_status remains complete.

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] TierPoint provides colocation, cloud, and managed IT services from a portfolio the company and its majority owner describe as roughly 40 data centers across about 18 to 20 U.S. markets. This session traced and dated the companys ownership structure, previously recorded without a clear citation chain: institutional investor Argo Infrastructure Partners began investing in TierPoint in 2020, added a further 500 million dollars in 2022, and took a majority stake by 2024. Per Argos own December 9, 2025 press release, Argo then acquired the equity interests of most of TierPoints remaining minority shareholders, consolidating its control and bringing total capital formation under Argos ownership to 3 billion dollars since 2020. Separately, per Data Center Dynamics trade press, Apollo Global Management announced in January 2025 that it would acquire Argo Infrastructure Partners itself, adding about 6 billion dollars in assets to Apollos infrastructure platform, with closing expected in the second quarter of 2025, meaning Argos majority stake in TierPoint now sits within Apollos broader infrastructure platform. This specific row, recorded simply as TierPoint in Saint Louis, MO, could not be confidently matched to a specific building this session. The operators own Missouri data centers page, fetched fresh this session, lists three distinct Saint Louis area facilities: Millpark, at 2315 Millpark Drive, Suite 104, Maryland Heights, MO 63043, roughly 12 miles west of downtown, Olive, at 1111 Olive Street, St. Louis, MO 63101, downtown, and Locust, at 2300 Locust Street, St. Louis, MO 63103, also downtown. This rows own coordinates place it within the downtown core, which reasonably rules out the Maryland Heights Millpark building, but do not reliably distinguish between the closely spaced downtown Olive and Locust buildings without a precise geocoding tool, which was not available this session. A Baxtel listing uses the URL slug cosentry-st-louis-olive for the Olive building, suggesting it carries the older, Cosentry heritage lineage, while Data Center Dynamics and local St. Louis Post-Dispatch coverage describe Locust as a newer, separately announced office to data center conversion project valued up to 150 million dollars. Given genuine ambiguity between two plausible, similarly downtown buildings, no specific address is asserted for this row. A future researcher with access to precise parcel level geocoding could likely resolve which of the Olive or Locust buildings this specific row represents.

reading.body:
This facility is a TierPoint colocation campus in downtown Saint Louis, Missouri. The operator publishes no power consumption figure for this site. TierPoint operates roughly 40 data centers across 18 to 20 U.S. markets as a colocation and managed services provider, now controlled by Apollo Global Management through its majority owner Argo Infrastructure Partners.

The specific building cannot be determined from available data. TierPoint lists three distinct Saint Louis area facilities: Millpark in Maryland Heights roughly 12 miles west of downtown, Olive at 1111 Olive Street downtown, and Locust at 2300 Locust Street also downtown. The coordinates provided place this row in the downtown core, ruling out Millpark but not distinguishing reliably between Olive and Locust without precise geocoding. A future researcher with parcel-level tools could likely resolve which building this row represents.

No published capacity figures exist for any TierPoint facility in Missouri or for this campus specifically. Missouri has eight mapped data center facilities on record with this site, none with published megawatt specifications. This campus therefore ranks first by published capacity in Missouri only because no other facility in the state has published a figure. Without a power specification, no assessment is possible of whether this campus matters to AI infrastructure scaling.
